comparison: Perfect agreement on identical substrate specificities of all four PP1-Phactr fusions (C4, C30-C33, C39-C41, C111). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and well-supported through multiple experimental approaches including immunoblotting, phosphoproteomics, and correlation analysis.

Complete agreement on the crystal structure quality and interpretation (C96-C103). Both accept the structural data showing PDZ-PBM interaction and absence of substrate-groove interactions. OpenEval notes the 2.36 Å resolution and appropriate reporting of unresolved regions; peer reviewers accepted without criticism.

Agreement on AlphaFold3 predictions (C104-C109). Both evaluations accept the computational modeling as supportive evidence. OpenEval appropriately notes these should be considered supportive rather than definitive; peer reviewers suggested additional modeling work but did not challenge existing predictions.

Strong agreement on 4E-BP as PP1-Neurabin substrate and link to mTORC1 signaling (C5, C50-C53, C56-C57, C60-C61, C116-C117, C126). Both evaluations view this as a major finding with converging evidence from phosphoproteomics, immunoblotting, in vitro assays, and functional translation assays. Peer review includes C131 not mentioned in OpenEval result.

Strong agreement on PDZ-mediated substrate recognition mechanism (C6, C71, C73-C74, C78-C79, C81-C83, C85, C94, C110). Both find compelling evidence that PDZ domain directs specificity rather than hydrophobic groove remodeling. Peer review includes additional claims C27, C62-C63, C70 related to the mechanism.

Both address PNUTS substrates (C45, C47, C113-C114). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative WDR82 recruitment mechanism lacking experimental validation. Peer reviewers SUPPORTED the findings as part of broader validation but did not extensively discuss the mechanistic speculation.

Agreement on differential substrate recognition mechanisms between Neurabin and Phactr families (C7, C95). Both accept the systematic mutagenesis evidence. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of peptide substitution effects; peer reviewers view the comparison as a key strength.

Partial overlap on substrate recognition mechanisms. OpenEval R4 addresses differential mechanisms (C7, C80, C84, C88-C92, C95) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R10 addresses subset of biochemical findings (C88-C93) also rated SUPPORTED, viewing them as supporting PDZ-driven vs groove-dependent specificity distinction.

Both address validation of PP1-PIP fusion approach (C25, C41). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on comparison with holoenzyme data and dose-response controls. Peer reviewers also SUPPORTED but with nuance: R3 strongly endorsed the approach while R4 cautioned it may not fully recapitulate holoenzyme regulation, introducing some uncertainty.

Both address negative results for PP1-GADD34/CReP (C44, C115). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting the negative result could reflect technical limitations and G-actin hypothesis remains untested. Peer reviewers also UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the result but not extensively discussing it; noted fusion approach limitations apply particularly here.

Minimal overlap on catalytic efficiency. OpenEval R14 addresses ~100-fold PIP enhancement and unexpected +1/+2 mutation effects (C86, C93) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R10 includes C93 as part of broader biochemical findings supporting distinct recognition mechanisms, also SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on C41 only. OpenEval R7 focuses on fusion protein validation methodology. Peer R1 focuses on Phactr substrate specificity findings. Both rate their respective claims as SUPPORTED but address largely different aspects.
Minimal overlap on C41 only. OpenEval R1 addresses Phactr substrate specificity. Peer R11 addresses fusion approach validation. Both SUPPORTED but focus on different claims despite sharing C41.

OpenEval R8 addresses phosphoproteomics methodology and validation (C34-C38) rated SUPPORTED, noting rigorous statistical analysis and enrichment for consensus motif. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these methodological claims.

OpenEval R11 addresses fluorescence polarization binding assays and 4E-BP isoform conservation (C64-C65, C72, C75) rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these binding affinity measurements.

OpenEval R12 addresses mutagenesis separating TOS and PBM functions (C66-C70) rated SUPPORTED, showing PBM importance for phosphatase recruitment independent of kinase recruitment. Peer R3 includes C70 but focuses on broader PDZ mechanism rather than TOS/PBM separation.

OpenEval R13 addresses lack of consensus motif across PIPs and distinct recognition mechanisms (C54-C55) rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing sequence analysis and motif diversity.

OpenEval R15 addresses speculation about Phactr functional differentiation through localization (C112) rated UNCERTAIN as untested hypothesis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this speculation.

OpenEval R16 addresses speculation about mTORC1-Neurabin competition for 4E-BP binding (C118) rated UNCERTAIN as plausible but untested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this competitive binding hypothesis.

OpenEval R17 addresses mechanistic model for processive dephosphorylation (C121-C122) rated UNCERTAIN as reasonable but lacking direct evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval R18 addresses speculation about broader PIP substrate recruitment mechanisms (C123-C125) rated UNCERTAIN as extrapolation requiring validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these broader mechanistic hypotheses.

Peer R7 addresses conserved RVxF-ΦΦ-R-W motif claims (C3, C16-C17, C19, C21) rated UNCERTAIN. Reviewer 1 challenged the W conservation, noting it's not conserved in sequence/structure across most PIPs discussed. No corresponding OpenEval result found specifically addressing this motif conservation claim.
